sections.content: How many people are "buyers and procurement officers"?

59,510 people

were counted on the census as "buyers and procurement officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Buyers and procurement officers organise and undertake the buying of raw materials, equipment and merchandise from manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and other sources for wholesale distribution, resale or for own internal use.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "buyers and procurement officers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "buyers and procurement officers", 16% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "buyers and procurement officers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "buyers and procurement officers" included:

  • youth work professionals
  • fitness and wellbeing instructors
  • project support officers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "buyers and procurement officers" there were a similar number of men and women (45.7% compared with 54.3%).

This means "buyers and procurement officers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 45.7% and women made up 54.3% of "buyers and procurement officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "buyers and procurement officers" included:

  • leisure and theme park attendants
  • business and related research professionals
  • estate agents and auctioneers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "buyers and procurement officers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "buyers and procurement officers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "buyers and procurement officers", 7.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82.8% compared with 17.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.6%) than self-employed (4.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
